name: HV/MV switchgear and site power distribution
principle: Medium-voltage switchgear receives, protects and distributes electrical power across a facility. Power arrives from utility infeed or site generation at high voltage (typically 132 kV and above for large plants), is transformed to a main distribution voltage (usually 11 kV or 33/36 kV onshore, 11 kV offshore), and flows through switchboards to transformers, motors and downstream boards. Air-insulated, gas-insulated (GIS) and hybrid designs exist; modern breakers use vacuum or SF6 interrupting technology.

process_steps.name: Incoming supply from utility infeed, generators or interconnector
Main switchboard switches, protects and meters the bus
Distribution transformers step down to LV or lower MV levels
Motor control centres and LV boards feed process loads
Downstream faults are cleared selectively by graded protection

performance.metric: IEC 62271-200 rated voltage range of metal-enclosed MV switchgear
performance.basis: IEC 62271-200 covers AC metal-enclosed switchgear and controlgear above 1 kV up to and including 52 kV

limitations: SF6 is a high-GWP gas under phasedown regulation, driving vacuum and dry-air alternatives
bus fault ratings and arc-flash containment need deliberate design at high fault levels
advantages: GIS suits confined offshore topsides and desert/urban substations
